subject: Acme POC - Integration plan & success criteria
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Carter <alex.carter@acme.com>, Maya Singh <maya.singh@acme.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Acme POC - Integration plan & success criteria

Hi Alex / Maya

Great call today thanks for the time. Per our discussion, here's a concise recap and the proposed integration / evaluation plan so your team can start scheduling work: 

1) Success criteria (what will define a successful POC)
- Latency: 95th percentile inference latency <= 350ms for 512-token requests (streaming allowed)
- Throughput: sustain 40 rps for batch inference during peak tests
- Quality: top-line accuracy on your internal intent classification eval >= 92% on the canonical prompt set (you sent sample prompts today)
- Stability: zero upstream failures during a 48h soak test, and graceful degradation to a smaller model variant under high load

2) Evaluation plan & timeline
- Week 0 (this week): access + onboarding, exchange keys, and confirm API routes and streaming handshake
- Week 1: integration of Redwood SDK, basic inference calls, run smoke tests against sample prompts
- Week 2: run load/soak tests and automated eval harness; iterate on prompt/temperature settings
- Week 3: joint review of metrics, decide on production readiness or next steps

3) Ownership
- Acme: Alex Carter (integration lead), Maya Singh (SRE) responsible for embedding SDK and running tests on your env
- Redwood: Marissa Cole (AE, POC owner) + Sean Gallagher (Solutions Eng) we will support integration, provide example code and debug issues

4) Integration notes / asks for your engineers
- We'll provide the Redwood SDK quickstart (attached) and a minimal example that uses streaming + tool-calling for richer responses.
- Please confirm the API routes you want us to validate against (e.g., /v1/generate, /v1/chat/stream) and whether you plan to use function/tool calling for external system lookups.
- Share a short list (10-50) of canonical prompts for the quality eval.

Attachments: acme_poc_requirements.xlsx (your ask matrix), acme_poc_success_criteria.pdf (summary).

Next steps: can we lock a 1-hour technical follow-up on Tue or Wed where Sean and I pair with your engineers? I've proposed times below.

Thanks
Marissa

Alex - perfect, thanks. I'm confirming the Wed 12 Aug 2026 10:00am PT slot for the deep technical session (invitation sent).

In advance of the call I'm sharing quick integration pointers and an implementation checklist (attached: redwood_sdk_quickstart.md, integration_checklist.csv):

- SDK quickstart: use our Python or Node SDK. Minimal example (Python streaming):

  from redwood import RedwoodClient
  client = RedwoodClient(api_key="REDACTED")
  with client.chat.stream(model="redwood-chat-1", messages=[{"role":"user","content":"<PROMPT>"}]) as stream:
      for chunk in stream:
          print(chunk.text, end="")

- API routes to validate: /v1/chat (sync), /v1/chat/stream (streaming), /v1/generate (batch/text-generation), /v1/embeddings
- Tool-calling: we support JSON schema-based functions. Best practice is to keep function responses small and fetch heavy payloads via a backend service your function calls. Example function schema sample will be in the repo link.
- Streaming tips: use low-latency websocket or server-sent events for real-time UI; set keepalive to avoid idle disconnects during long responses.
- Quantization / model variants: we'll provide two model profiles - high-throughput quantized variant and high-quality FP16 variant. For soak testing use the quantized profile first.

I've also included a short eval script in the GitHub repo for running your canonical prompts and producing a CSV of metrics (accuracy, response time, token usage). Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/acme-poc/tree/main

Let me know if the eng-lead would like temporary sandbox credentials and we'll provision a short-lived API key and a shared test project.

Cheers,
Marissa
